meta.title: Spatial Strategy Playbook — evidence base
meta.how_to_use: The strategy generator may only cite entries from this file. 'proven_cases' have published, measured outcomes. 'reference_examples' are design precedents with no published results and must be labeled 'precedent, no published results'. 'research' entries are industry-wide findings. 'principles' are spatial rules with their sources. Every recommendation the generator makes must point to at least one id from proven_cases or research; anything else is labeled 'untested idea'.

evidence_strength_scale.third_party_data: Measured by an independent data provider (e.g. Placer.ai foot traffic) or independent research body.
evidence_strength_scale.company_reported: Figures published by the brand or retailer (press release, earnings call, newsroom).
evidence_strength_scale.agency_reported: Figures published by the agency or practitioner that produced the work.
evidence_strength_scale.directional: Outcome described without a precise figure, or growth not directly attributed to the store experience.

proven_cases.project: House of Sport experiential store format
proven_cases.what_they_did: Built stores around places to play and test gear, such as climbing walls and batting cages, rather than racks of product alone.

results.metric: Visits per location against the chain average
results.value: about 5 to 6x
Still growing three to four years after opening, with longer visits and bigger baskets than at standard DICK'S stores (CEO, Q1 2026 call)

proven_cases.lesson: Space given to trying and playing earns its square footage when it pulls repeat visits; the play zone is the destination that drives traffic through the store.

sources.title: Dick's Sporting Goods: New Store Formats Driving Visit Outperformance
Dick's continues to reap the gains from its experiential stores

proven_cases.project: Tabby global activations and AR storefront (SoHo, with ZERO10)
proven_cases.location: New York SoHo; Tokyo, Bangkok, Singapore and others
proven_cases.what_they_did: Put an AR mirror in the SoHo store window and ran Tabby pop ups with cafés, ice cream trucks, immersive rooms, and local artist murals.

results.metric: More pedestrians paying attention than to a standard window
More store traffic with the AR window
Gen Z share of Tabby visitors in North America
results.value: 95%, with waits of 60 to 75 minutes and visits of about 9 minutes

proven_cases.lesson: An interactive window can measurably convert passersby into store visitors when it lets people try the product on themselves.

sources.title: How Coach used global retail activations to popularize a hero product

proven_cases.what_they_did: Redesigned stores around experience and customization, paused the rollout to study shopper feedback, then relaunched.

results.value: Higher traffic and longer visits, strongest with Gen Z (no figure published)
The concept will cover 80% of Coach store traffic by fiscal 2030

proven_cases.lesson: Test a store concept, pause to learn from shoppers, then scale; customization is part of making the store 'as engaging as the product'.

sources.title: Tapestry leverages customer insights to court Gen Z in Coach stores

proven_cases.project: Samsung Experience Store, Il Centro di Arese (Milan)
proven_cases.format: brand experience store in a mall
proven_cases.what_they_did: Hands on ecosystem demos, free data transfer between devices, colours sold only in store, technical support, workshops, and live demonstrations.

results.value: About half of buyers added another Samsung device

proven_cases.lesson: For a tech brand, a setup-and-transfer service plus ecosystem demos turns a single purchase into a multi-device basket.

sources.title: Samsung Experience Store di Arese first anniversary (Italian)

proven_cases.what_they_did: Placed Sephora shops inside Kohl's stores, with small formats grouped by category rather than by brand.

results.value: Over $1.4 billion

results.metric: Share of Kohl's sales growth over the year
results.value: More than 90%

proven_cases.lesson: A destination category placed inside a partner's store can bring that partner new customers; small formats work when curated by shopper need.
proven_cases.caveats: Source article is undated (published around 2023). Later Retail Dive coverage (2025) reports Sephora at Kohl's sales slowing, so treat as a growth-phase result.

sources.title: Sephora at Kohl's Sales Reach $1.4 Billion, 140 New Stores Planned

proven_cases.project: Two week pop up at Future Stores, Oxford Street (with Dalziel & Pow)
proven_cases.what_they_did: Treated a bank like a hospitality brand, with a matcha bar, a Wisdom Bar for specialist advice, streetwear style merch kiosks that rewarded new accounts, and an event space.

results.value: Nearly 16,000
1 million+

proven_cases.lesson: Borrowing hospitality cues from outside the category makes a low-interest category worth visiting; tie a reward to the action you want (sign-ups).

sources.title: Brand rebellion: how to stand out by breaking up with category conventions

proven_cases.what_they_did: A speakeasy behind a hidden door in a Swedish bodega, with one room for each sleep essential (comfort, sound, air, light, organization, and temperature), QR purchasing throughout, and themed food and scent.

results.value: Highest attendance of any NYC IKEA event
IKEA plans to bring elements into permanent stores

proven_cases.lesson: Organize an experience around the shopper's problem (sleep) rather than product categories; a pop-up can prototype ideas for permanent stores.

sources.title: IKEA's Dreamy 'Sleepeasy' Is a Whimsical Ode to a Good Night's Sleep

proven_cases.project: Store events powered by loyalty data
proven_cases.what_they_did: Made its loyalty program the main data source for AI personalization and ran more than 100,000 store events.

results.value: 46.7 million (up 5% in fiscal 2025)
Events lifted store conversion and NPS (no figure published)

proven_cases.lesson: Events at scale, informed by loyalty data, are a lever on store conversion, not only on awareness.

sources.title: AI Helps Retailers Bring Digital Personalization to Physical Stores

proven_cases.project: ReBird repair, trade in, and resale
proven_cases.what_they_did: Trade in for store credit, repairs down to whole panel replacement, care events, and upcycling, with a repair center in SoHo.

results.metric: Units traded in over the first six months

results.value: 30% of retail price (up from 20%)

proven_cases.lesson: Service and repair give owners a reason to return after the sale and make product quality visible.

sources.title: 'Education is key': Outdoor apparel brand Arc'teryx grows its circularity program

proven_cases.brand: CVS Health (and other retail media networks)
proven_cases.what_they_did: Screens at the entrance, the pharmacy wait, the end caps, and the checkout, with about 11,000 expected in 2026.

results.metric: Shoppers who find the screens useful
Shoppers who act after seeing them

proven_cases.lesson: Screens help where shoppers wait or decide (pharmacy, checkout); placed elsewhere they become clutter. Note the contrast with the 'tech woven into architecture' direction.

sources.title: Retailers like Kroger, CVS plan many more screens for in-store ads in 2026

proven_cases.format: small format (IKEA London, Ont.: 43,000 sq ft, ~2,700 items)
proven_cases.what_they_did: Opened stores at a fraction of the usual size, with a tighter range, in dense city neighborhoods.

results.metric: Time to open against a full size store
results.value: 25% faster, at lower cost
IKEA closed its small Scarborough store within three years, citing online shopping and a limited range

proven_cases.lesson: Small formats are cheaper and faster but live or die on the edit; plan what earns floor space.

sources.title: Why retailers like Ikea are going big on small stores

proven_cases.project: Nike Live / Well Collective neighborhood stores (cautionary case)
proven_cases.what_they_did: Opened hyperlocal neighborhood stores in 2018 beside its flagships and renamed them Well Collective in 2023. In 2026 Nike closed at least 15 and moved community concepts to partners such as Crenshaw Rec by Foot Locker.

results.value: At least 15 neighborhood stores closed by August 2026
150+ stores elevated with sport experiences (CEO Elliott Hill)

proven_cases.lesson: The community tier is the hardest to sustain alone; partner-run community stores and upgraded flagships are Nike's current answer.

sources.title: Nike is quietly closing its localized neighborhood stores

proven_cases.what_they_did: Runs stores as exhibitions built around large kinetic sculptures, refreshes them like galleries, and adds brand collaborations.

results.value: 789.1 billion won, nearly 4x four years earlier
29.6%, with about 40% of revenue from overseas

proven_cases.lesson: Installation-led stores can be the brand's main awareness engine; growth is credited to showrooms, collaborations and social media together, not to stores alone.

sources.title: K-Eyewear on the Rise

research.finding: Opening a store raised a retailer's web traffic by 37% on average. Closing one cut web traffic in that market by 9.5% for apparel, 7.9% for department stores, and 16.4% for home goods.

source.title: ICSC says there's a 'halo effect' by retailers having physical stores

research.caveats: Older study (2016–2018 data); use as directional support for the store's role in omnichannel.

research.finding: Fitness tenants drive 4.2 visits per visitor each month, and 90.8% of those visits last over 30 minutes. From 2019 to 2025 coffee visits grew 26.7% and spa visits 31.8%, while apparel visits fell nearly 25%.

source.title: Placer.ai: Fitness, service tenants drive visits, dwell times at shopping centers

research.finding: 80% of shopping still happens in stores. Nearly two thirds of shoppers want to see and touch products before they buy, and nearly half will pay extra to pick up within 10 minutes of home.
research.framework: Five faces of the store: product-focused, service-focused, experiential/showroom, fulfillment/omnichannel, brand & community builder.

source.title: Future-proof your stores: Adapting physical spaces for a digital-first world

research.finding: Camera analytics cost about a tenth of what they did three years ago. A 2026 retail technology report lists VR shopping, metaverse activations, chatbot service for complex purchases, and fully autonomous stores outside busy formats as not working.

source.title: Retail Technology Trends 2026: What's Actually Working in Stores

reference_examples.what: NYC flagship Magic Wall. A few strides of gait analysis and a depth camera foot scan pick the model and size, and an advisor brings the pair from storage behind the wall.
Zurich Movement Lab table. Clouds part as you approach, and lifting a shoe plays a film on its materials. The table is brushed steel to match the store.

House of Innovation NYC, 68,000 sq ft. An atrium sound and video installation called Arena, a customization counter, a members only Expert Studio, a basement Speed Shop with pickup lockers, and mobile checkout.

Nike Rise Seoul, about 24,000 sq ft. A motion reactive LED entrance, a three story Sport Pulse screen with live city activity, a huddle area for local events, repair and recycling, and tees by local artists.
Soho flagship redesign around a kinetic sculpture of three hyperreal faces, an interactive sculpture, and a central LED sphere.
Charm Garden residency at the Corner Shop, with a Rexy slide sized for adults, an apple photo booth, a giant Tabby monogramming station, and a charm residency by tattoo artists.
Corner Shop training studio, with an AI installation that turned movement into digital art, run clubs, and fitness and life drawing classes.

reference_examples.brand: Uniqlo, Capital One, Aritzia, Ralph Lauren
reference_examples.what: Cafés inside stores, from Uniqlo Fifth Avenue (2025) and more than 60 Capital One cafés that host classes to Aritzia's cafés and Ralph's Coffee Newport (2026).
Quiet Hours, with lower music, dimmer light, and quieter screens, piloted in 32 stores across 8 markets and then rolled out worldwide.
Official shoe partner of Camp Flog Gnaw, the festival of Tyler, the Creator, in its tenth year (2024), within a collaboration of about seven years.
Rig Advisor, an AI assistant launched by QR code that recommends gear stocked in that store.
Nike Rise Seoul's entrance. A tunnel of screens by the door responds to movement and lights up as each shopper walks in.

principles.rule: Keep the first 5 to 15 ft clear of signage and key product.
Put the hero product and key message on the first wall to the right, where most visitors turn.
People buy what they can handle. Keep the hero product out from behind glass.
Give browsing zones generous aisles. Shoppers jostled from behind two or three times tend to leave.
Plan short pauses, product interaction, and longer stays as separate zones.
Separate fast missions such as pickup from slow ones such as consultation and customization.
Measure dwell by zone, paths, and queues after opening. Camera analytics now cost about a tenth of what they did three years ago.
Anchor the window on one hero piece with room around it, and make sure it reads from the sidewalk by day and after dark.
Navigate by landmark rather than signs. One visible feature orients the whole floor.
Keep one zone on modular fixtures, so launches, classes, and residencies need no rebuild.
Research the neighborhood first, from nearby businesses to listening sessions with locals, and then edit a small store's range to match.
